maintainer: CSOAI Ltd — claim maintenance (measurement, never certification)

supersedes.rule: supersede by reference, never edit: the prior file's bytes are unchanged, still served at their own URL, and still covered by whatever signature and timestamp receipt they had

superseded_because: The visible-text digests of the prior registry were taken by csoai-visible-text/1, the extractor of the v0.1 reference, which departed from spec 6.3 step 2 (spec v0.2 section 16). This revision re-reads every visible-text source once, re-baselines its digest under csoai-visible-text/2 and names that extractor in the artifact (spec v0.2 5.6.1). Nothing in it says any subject's page changed except where rule 1, compared with itself, says so; those are listed under extractor_rebaseline and recorded as observed changes in neutral words.

extractor_rebaseline.method: one live read per distinct URL from this host; both extractors applied to the same response bytes; rule 1 today compared with the recorded rule-1 digest (like with like), and rule 2 today compared with rule 1 today (same bytes, different reader). Every classification below is that comparison, not an estimate.

classifications.UNCHANGED_SAME_UNDER_BOTH_RULES: the page is unchanged since capture under rule 1, and the two rules agree on it
classifications.UNCHANGED_EXTRACTOR_DIFFERS: the page is unchanged since capture under rule 1, and rule 2 extracts different text from the same bytes. A watcher that switched rules silently would have recorded each of these as an observed change. They are a change of reader, not of page, and are recorded as none (spec v0.2 6.3.1)
classifications.CHANGED_AT_SOURCE_SINCE_CAPTURE: rule 1 today differs from the recorded rule-1 digest: compared like with like, the page differs from the capture. Recorded as an observed change in the artifact, naming rule 1
classifications.RULE_1_CANNOT_READ: rule 1 throws on today's bytes, so no like-with-like comparison exists and none is asserted
classifications.NOT_REREAD: the page could not be obtained from this host; the recorded rule-1 digest is carried unchanged

does_not_prove: that any page changed where the classification is UNCHANGED_EXTRACTOR_DIFFERS; it did not, under the rule that recorded it
why any page changed where one did; a subject may change its website for any reason (spec 4.9)
that the counts above describe any page as served on a day other than the read_utc recorded per row

selection_rule: Platforms on which an AI agent engages a human to perform a task, or a human engages an agent, and which publish a machine interface for it (an MCP server, a REST API or an x402 resource). Three were named to this lane (RentAHuman, gotoHuman, Payman); two more were added from third-party indexes: Invoke, because the official MCP registry lists a hosted server for it that describes hiring a human, and InstaHuman, because it is one of four hosts in the two public x402 discovery indexes whose resource descriptions offer work done by a person, and the only one of the four whose own page describes a marketplace of paid human workers engaged by agents. Both publish their own site and terms. Candidates were dropped where the operator is a single natural person (humanforai.dev, yourhuman.ai, missionforhire.com), because a measurement of such a subject is a measurement of a person, or where the service is not a hiring platform on its own page (human4ai.ai, parahuman.co). Within each subject the claims selected are those specific enough to capture verbatim and about something a worker, an agent operator or a regulator would rely on: headcount, interfaces, payment rails, escrow and dispute, identity checks, worker classification and the operating entity. Where a subject states a limit on what it does, that statement is captured on the same footing as any other claim, because a scoped claim is a result and not an absence. No person is named, and no personal data is captured.

capture_notes_explained: For every claim: how this reader located the claim string inside what it read, and on which surface. EXACT means byte-for-byte in the extracted text. MATCHED_AFTER_NORMALISING_EXTRACTOR_ARTEFACTS means the string is there once this extractor's own stray spaces before punctuation and its inline footnote markers are removed. A reader of the page sees neither, and the specification anticipates that extractors differ and asks for exactly this disclosure (spec 6.3). MATCHED_IN_DOCUMENT_TEXT_LAYER means the source is a filed document whose published digest covers its bytes, and the sentence was located in the text layer extracted from those bytes. EXACT_IN_RESPONSE_BYTES means the source is plain text with no extractor between the bytes and the reader, so the string is in the same bytes the digest covers. The mode is published rather than normalised away, so a reader can tell an extractor difference from a content change. In this revision every re-read visible-text claim was located in text extracted by csoai-visible-text/2, and its mode at first capture is kept beside it as located_at_first_capture.

merkle.split: largest power of two strictly below n
merkle.odd_leaf_handling: none — no duplication and no carry-up; the split rule handles every n
merkle.entry_bytes: canonical JSON of the claim artifact (spec 6.1: keys sorted by code point, no insignificant whitespace, UTF-8, no floating-point numbers), with the sig field omitted
merkle.leaf_order: the order of the claims array in this file
merkle.not_the_other_root: This is NOT the estate public card root at /root.json. That root duplicates an odd final node and uses no domain-separation prefixes; it is a separate structure over a separate corpus and the two are never added, reconciled or substituted for one another (spec 7.3).

boundaries: No claim of falsity is made about any party, anywhere in this file. Where a measurement differs from a claim, the claim, the measured value, the window, the denominator and the method are recorded and nothing further is said. The reader draws the conclusion; this maintainer does not.
A listing here is not an endorsement and it is not an accusation. It means a public page is being read on a schedule.

Nothing here is a finding about the employment status of any worker, the lawfulness of any platform, or the adequacy of any human oversight. Statements a subject makes about worker classification, identity checks, escrow or dispute resolution are captured as that subject's statements; the only bodies that can settle the first of those are courts and tribunals, and none of their records was read.

Every source was read without a key, an account or a payment. No account was created, no form was submitted, no task was posted and no payment was made. A source that required a token was dropped and recorded in the harness output, never worked around.

A page or register this reader could not obtain is SEARCH_INCONCLUSIVE with its HTTP status recorded. It is never recorded as an absence. The code host answers 404 both for a repository that does not exist and for a private one, so a 404 there is read as neither.
A /.well-known file that is PRESENT is evidence that the file was published and nothing more; what it says is the subject speaking again. Where this lane read one, it is used only as that.

No personal data is carried. Package-registry maintainer names and e-mail addresses, and the street address and telephone number on a regulator's filer record, were present in bytes that were read and hashed; they are not reproduced here.

The maintainer publishes its own MCP servers in the official MCP registry and its own x402 resources in the same discovery indexes read here. That is co-listing in a public index, not a relationship with any subject, and it is stated so a reader can weigh it.

See /claims/claimreg-hiring-platforms-2026-09-24-rev2.signed.json, which pins this file by sha256 and carries the Ed25519 signature by did:web:csoai.org#board-attestation-1. A signature proves these bytes were signed at that time; it grades nothing, certifies nobody, and says nothing about any party named here (spec 9.5).
timestamp_state: SUBMITTED, and therefore PENDING. An OpenTimestamps receipt is written beside this file at /claims/claimreg-hiring-platforms-2026-09-24-rev2.json.ots. At the time of writing it carries a calendar commitment and no attestation path, its upgrade has not been run, and nothing has been verified. The specification reserves a third word for a receipt that has been upgraded AND whose path has been checked, and that word is not used of this receipt (spec 8.1-8.3). A file extension is not a proof.
